children: agreed to acquire Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock transaction that values the optical networking company at approximately $1,132 per share.
Marvell shares slipped about 5% in the morning session.

The proposed terms give Lumentum investors roughly 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own. Once completed, Marvell shareholders are expected to hold 67% of the combined business, with the remaining 33% belonging to Lumentum investors. The offer represents a 23.9% premium to the companies' closing prices on Oct. 28.

The transaction would expand Marvell's presence in optical connectivity for AI infrastructure. The companies estimate the combined business will have a potential addressable market of $550 billion and generate more than $1 billion in annual cost savings and other synergies.

Marvell will retain leadership of the combined company, with CEO Matt Murphy at the helm. Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston will join an expanded board. The deal is targeted for completion in the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

title: Why Marvell Stock Is Tumbling Today
